## Specialty Nursing (Emergency – Standard Option), Bachelor of Science in Nursing

- **Credential:** Bachelor of Science in Nursing  
- **Study mode:** Part-time  
- **Delivery:** Fully online  
- **School:** School of Health Sciences  
- **Total credits:** 60.0  
- **Status:** Active  

The program is designed for registered nurses and focuses on emergency nursing theory, clinical practice, leadership, community nursing, and professional development.

### Curriculum

**Required emergency nursing courses**

- **NSCC 7150 — Dysrhythmia Interpretation and Management** — 2 credits  
- **NSER 7110 — Emergency Nursing Theory 1** — 4 credits  
- **NSER 7210 — Emergency Nursing Theory 2** — 4 credits  
- **NSER 7300 — Emergency Nursing Clinical 1** — 5 credits  
- **NSER 7410 — Emergency Nursing Theory 3** — 4 credits  
- **NSER 7500 — Emergency Nursing Clinical 2** — 5 credits  

**Core and management component — 21 credits**

- **BUSA 7250 — Management Skills and Applications** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 7115 — Teaching and Learning in Specialty Nursing** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 8000 — Systematic Inquiry** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 8300 — Creative Leadership** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 8500 — Professional Growth** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 8600 — Community Nursing: Facilitating Health** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 8800 — Community Nursing: Facilitating Health Action** — 3 credits  

**Liberal Studies component — 12 credits**

Required courses:

- **COMM 7100 — Intercultural Communication Competency and Diversity Awareness for Professionals** — 3 credits  
- **LIBS 7021 — Health Ethics** — 3 credits  

The remaining 6 credits are General Education electives at the 100-level minimum, from at least two academic disciplines.

**Approved elective pool**

You must complete **at least 3 credits from the approved pool**, rather than a fixed number of courses:

- **NSER 7250 — Advanced Cardiac Life Support** — 1 credit  
- **NSER 7800 — Emergency Nursing and Mental Health** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 8130 — Independent Study in Specialty Nursing** — 3 credits  

The curriculum also notes that Program Head-approved emergency-nursing electives may be used, including options such as TNCC, ENPC, ATLS, NRP, or PALS.

### Admission requirements

The published admission requirements include:

- English Studies 12 at **73% or equivalent**
- A post-secondary diploma in nursing
- Current practicing RN registration with the BCCNM, a Canadian provincial equivalent, or an RN licence number if practising outside Canada
- At least **six months of acute-care work experience**
- A resume of work experience

The program also lists clinical requirements such as current qualifying CPR certification, proof of professional registration for clinical courses, respirator fit testing, and compliance with the influenza immunization-or-masking policy. These clinical requirements require institutional confirmation.

International applicants may complete the program from outside Canada or with a valid Canadian work permit covering the clinical-training period. The program states that international applicants are not eligible for a study permit or a post-graduation work permit through this program. International applicants must receive Program Head approval before applying.

For the latest details, see the [official program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-emergency-standard-option-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810bbsn/).

conversation.user: Who should I confirm my situation with?
conversation.advisor:
Please confirm your situation with the **Specialty Nursing Program Head** before applying. This is especially important because international applicants require Program Head approval, and the Program Head can assess questions about:

- Whether your nursing experience qualifies, including acute-care experience or any recency concerns
- Your RN registration or licence
- Clinical-placement requirements
- Whether you can complete the program from outside Canada or with your existing Canadian work permit

You should also contact **BCIT International** for immigration-related guidance, but the program states that it does **not** make international students eligible for a Canadian study permit or PGWP.

[Official program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-emergency-standard-option-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810bbsn/)

## Specialty Nursing (Emergency – Standard Option), Bachelor of Science in Nursing

- **Credential:** Bachelor of Science in Nursing  
- **Study mode:** Part-time  
- **Delivery:** Fully online  
- **School:** School of Health Sciences  
- **Total credits:** 60.0  
- **Status:** Active  

The program is designed for registered nurses and focuses on emergency nursing theory, clinical practice, leadership, community nursing, and professional development.

### Curriculum

**Required emergency nursing courses**

- **NSCC 7150 — Dysrhythmia Interpretation and Management** — 2 credits  
- **NSER 7110 — Emergency Nursing Theory 1** — 4 credits  
- **NSER 7210 — Emergency Nursing Theory 2** — 4 credits  
- **NSER 7300 — Emergency Nursing Clinical 1** — 5 credits  
- **NSER 7410 — Emergency Nursing Theory 3** — 4 credits  
- **NSER 7500 — Emergency Nursing Clinical 2** — 5 credits  

**Core and management component — 21 credits**

- **BUSA 7250 — Management Skills and Applications** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 7115 — Teaching and Learning in Specialty Nursing** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 8000 — Systematic Inquiry** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 8300 — Creative Leadership** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 8500 — Professional Growth** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 8600 — Community Nursing: Facilitating Health** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 8800 — Community Nursing: Facilitating Health Action** — 3 credits  

**Liberal Studies component — 12 credits**

Required courses:

- **COMM 7100 — Intercultural Communication Competency and Diversity Awareness for Professionals** — 3 credits  
- **LIBS 7021 — Health Ethics** — 3 credits  

The remaining 6 credits are General Education electives at the 100-level minimum, from at least two academic disciplines.

**Approved elective pool**

You must complete **at least 3 credits from the approved pool**, rather than a fixed number of courses:

- **NSER 7250 — Advanced Cardiac Life Support** — 1 credit  
- **NSER 7800 — Emergency Nursing and Mental Health** — 3 credits  
- **NSSC 8130 — Independent Study in Specialty Nursing** — 3 credits  

The curriculum also notes that Program Head-approved emergency-nursing electives may be used, including options such as TNCC, ENPC, ATLS, NRP, or PALS.

### Admission requirements

The published admission requirements include:

- English Studies 12 at **73% or equivalent**
- A post-secondary diploma in nursing
- Current practicing RN registration with the BCCNM, a Canadian provincial equivalent, or an RN licence number if practising outside Canada
- At least **six months of acute-care work experience**
- A resume of work experience

The program also lists clinical requirements such as current qualifying CPR certification, proof of professional registration for clinical courses, respirator fit testing, and compliance with the influenza immunization-or-masking policy. These clinical requirements require institutional confirmation.

International applicants may complete the program from outside Canada or with a valid Canadian work permit covering the clinical-training period. The program states that international applicants are not eligible for a study permit or a post-graduation work permit through this program. International applicants must receive Program Head approval before applying.

For the latest details, see the [official program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-emergency-standard-option-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810bbsn/).

This policy affects all students who will be entering a clinical setting. As such, you will be required to provide proof of your immunization or agree to wear a mask at all times prior to being placed in your clinical studies. Students are expected to carry their certificate with them at all times during their practicum. For the Respirator Fit Testing, fit testing with a N95 respirator (1860, 1860s, or 1870) is required and must be performed, in accordance with CSA Standard CAN/CSA-Z94.4-02. Fit Testing must also include inspection, cleaning, maintenance, and storage of protective equipment. Students will be given specific instructions in preparation for their fit testing by the provider they choose.
